broken_signatures.case: lat mot bit trong nua Ed25519
broken_signatures.why: classical half broken — the whole signature must fail

broken_signatures.case: lat mot bit trong nua ML-DSA
broken_signatures.why: post-quantum half broken — the whole signature must fail
the last byte must be covered by verification too
a missing byte must be a length error, not a pass
longer than specified must also fail
the byte layout is part of the standard

description: Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signatures. The most important interop group after `canonical`. Checked in three directions — key generation, signing, verification — because verifying our signatures is not enough if you produce signatures we cannot verify. See FORMAT.md.

external_anchor.notes: The Ed25519 half is anchored to RFC 8032 §7.1 TEST 1 — external to this project and checkable by anyone. The ML-DSA-65 half is anchored to NIST ACVP; see acvp-mldsa65.json.

algorithm.rule: BOTH halves must be valid. One half passing is not enough.

independent_crosscheck.conclusion: Two independent FIPS 204 implementations produce the SAME signature, byte for byte.

second_implementation.type: pure Python, sharing not one line of code with ml-dsa (Rust)

independent_crosscheck.why_needed: ACVP vectors anchor keyGen and sigVer but CANNOT anchor the signing direction: they supply expanded secret keys, which this implementation cannot load. A second implementation was the only route left.
independent_crosscheck.prerequisite: The Python side must match the NIST vectors FIRST (25/25 keyGen). Without that step it is merely a second opinion — two implementations wrong in the same way still agree with each other.
